---
title: "FPC function"
description: >-
  Visualizing the Finite Population Correction factor and its impact on standard
  error when sampling without replacement.
categories: [Tutorial, Stats]
---

```{python}
#| label: fpc

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def _():
  # --- setup ---
  N = 1000                      # population size
  sigma = 50                    # population standard deviation
  n = np.arange(1, N + 1)       # sample sizes
  f = n / N                     # sampling fraction

# --- finite population correction factor ---
  fpc = np.sqrt((N - n) / (N - 1))

# --- standard error of the mean ---
  se_without = sigma / np.sqrt(n)
  se_with    = se_without * fpc

# --- plot ---
  fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 9))

# 1. FPC vs sampling fraction
  ax[0].plot(f, fpc, color='steelblue', lw=2)
  ax[0].axhline(1, color='gray', linestyle='--', lw=1)
  ax[0].set_xlabel('Sampling fraction n / N')
  ax[0].set_ylabel('Finite Population Correction factor')
  ax[0].set_title(
      r'FPC$(n) = \sqrt{\dfrac{N-n}{N-1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1000-n}{999}}$'
  )
  ax[0].set_xlim(0, 1)
  ax[0].set_ylim(0, 1.1)
  ax[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Standard error with vs without FPC
  ax[1].plot(f, se_without,
             label=r'Without FPC:  $SE(n) = \dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} = \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{n}}$',
             color='coral', lw=2)
  ax[1].plot(f, se_with,
             label=r'With FPC:  $SE(n) = \dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}\sqrt{\dfrac{N-n}{N-1}} = \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{n}}\sqrt{\dfrac{1000-n}{999}}$',
             color='steelblue', lw=2)
  ax[1].set_xlabel('Sampling fraction n / N')
  ax[1].set_ylabel('Standard error of the mean')
  ax[1].set_title(
      r'$SE(n) = \dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$ vs. '
      r'$SE(n)\cdot\sqrt{\dfrac{N-n}{N-1}}$   (overstatement without FPC)'
  )
  ax[1].legend()
  ax[1].set_xlim(0, 1)
  ax[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

  plt.tight_layout()
  plt.show()

_()
```
